# Description

- `before`
  - I corrected the part where the return type was defined as the assigned function, even though it returns a new function.
- `once`:
  - Previously, the function was designed to only accept functions without arguments, but we needs to accept functions with arguments. So I added this feature.
  - I simplified the code a bit.

comments.body:
```suggestion
function before<F extends (...args: any[]) => any>(
```

Actually, since parameters are contravariant, we have to specify `never` or `any` in the parameters to ensure that `F` can be any function.

```suggestion
- `func` (`F extends (...args: any[]) => any`): 一度だけ呼び出すように制限する関数です。
```

```suggestion
export function once<F extends () => any>(func: F): () => ReturnType<F> {
```
I think `func` should be a function accepting no arguments.

```suggestion
- `func` (`F extends () => any`): 要限制的函数。
```

```suggestion
- `func` (`F extends () => any`): The function to restrict.
```
If `func` is a function accepting no arguments, why can't `once` just return `F` here?
Thanks to review!

> I think `func` should be a function accepting no arguments.


I modified it because if it doesn’t accept parameters, it would be inconvenient to write something like:
```javascript
const onced = once(console.log);
onced("hello")
```
Is there a specific reason the interface is different from `before`?
Also, even if the interface is updated, it shouldn’t cause any issues with backward compatibility.

> If `func` is a function accepting no arguments, why can't `once` just return `F` here?

I’ve applied this to the code. Thank you!

When searching through the use cases of `once`, I think there are two usecases:

**[1] Ensuring that we initialize certain objects only once, like:**

```tsx
const createClient = once(() => new Client());

createClient();
createClient(); // client is created only once
```

**[2] Ensuring that we make a side effect only once, like:**

```tsx
const log = once(console.log);

log('hello')
log('world') // this call is ignored
```

But I guess [1] is covered with [memoize](https://es-toolkit.slash.page/reference/function/memoize.html#memoize), so `once` might focus on solving the problem [2].

If we were to support [2], we might restrict the function to return `void` when it receives parameters, like:

```tsx
export function once<F extends (...args: any) => void>(func: F): F;
```

> If we were to support [2], we might restrict the function to return `void` when it receives parameters, like:
> 
> ```tsx
> export function once<F extends () => any>(func: F): F;
> export function once<F extends (...args: any) => void>(func: F): F;
> ```

Oh, if we change it like this, the function’s role will become much clearer!

> But since we need backward compatibility, the best option we can choose might be supporting both:
> 
> ```tsx
> export function once<F extends () => any>(func: F): F;
> export function once<F extends (...args: any) => void>(func: F): F;
> ```

I added these suggestions to the code.
